newsitem.title: UK: Record payout for boss fired by Rentokil.
newsitem.headline: Record payout for boss fired by Rentokil.

text.p: The high-flying executive who helped turn around business services group BET only to be fired after it was bought by Rentokil earlier this year won 3 million British pounds ($4.5 million) in compensation Wednesday.

The award to U.S.-born John Clark by a High Court judge was thought to be the highest ever in Britain in a wrongful dismissal case. It was four times the amount offered as a pre-trial settlement but only half what Clark had sought.
Rentokil, the pest-control-to-security group that recently changed its name to Rentokil Initial Plc, immediately said it would appeal the ruling.
A Rentokil spokesman said it was "an absolutely enormous sum of money, and clearly we are going to appeal."
Clark alleged that Rentokil had wrongfully dismissed him after its hostile 2.2 billion pound ($3.5 billion) takeover of BET Plc in April.
"I am very pleased with the outcome," Clark told reporters. "The sums recovered represent what the court has held to be the strict entitlement under my contract and no more."
"I regret it was necessary to bring my claim to court. I normally seek to resolve such matters in a private and mature manner."
Clark, described by the judge as "an extremely able, energetic and successful businessman," was recruited by BET in 1991.
He transformed the group's fortunes but was ousted after Rentokil gained majority control of BET in the takeover bid.
Clark told reporters he was now eager to continue his search for a position as chief executive in a major organisation.
